title: Prefill handshake microbench adapter for rapid kernel preference profiling
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: when a new model instance comes online or a request pattern shifts (bursty prefill-heavy flows), our static kernel selection heuristics sometimes pick suboptimal attention/attention-variant kernels (e.g. flash vs triton matmul paths), which increases decode tail latency or token cost for medium token lengths (32-256). Background: existing autotuners run longer explorations or are offline; we need a low-latency, safe runtime probe that quickly produces a per-instance kernel preference vector. Proposal: implement a lightweight 'prefill handshake microbench adapter' that runs short microbenchmarks at instance startup and periodically during idle windows.
Key behaviors: 1) Execute a bounded set of synthetic mini-prefill and mini-decode runs across a compact matrix of (kernel implementation, seq-len bucket, beam/greedy flag, dtype/quantization profile) with strict runtime budgets (e.g. <= 200ms total wall time, <= 10% spare GPU occupancy). 2) Compute a tiny score (latency, variance, tokens/sec, and estimated cost-per-token) and synthesize an ordered preference list saved in instance metadata and surfaced to the routing layer. 3) Respect safety: run at low priority, abort on contention metrics (GPU util, SLO pressure), rate limit by instance age and by customer tier. 4) TTL the profile and re-probe adaptively when request distributions change (drift detection via seq-len histogram divergence). Rationale: short, targeted probes provide immediate, actionable kernel preferences for early traffic and bursty flows without running expensive, long-running autotune experiments. This reduces tail latency for common mid-length prefill patterns and gives better decode cost for mixed workloads.
Implementation notes:
- Microbench harness lives in runtime/prober with a small C++/Rust microbench runner calling the same kernels as production paths to avoid bias.
- Use deterministic synthetic inputs (seeded token sequences) and lightweight KV cache warmup to emulate prefill vs decode.
- Buckets: {8, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512} for prefill; decode probes use short prefix lengths (1-16) to evaluate per-token overhead.
- Scoring: primary objective is p95 latency on prefill; secondary is decode per-token latency and estimated cost.
- Persisted artifact: a compact JSON preference vector (kernel ids ordered) plus probing metadata (timestamp, seqlen_hist_anchor, probe_version).
Rollout plan: gated rollout to non-production fleets, manual verification, then progressive ramp to production with feature flag per-cluster.
Integration: routing will consult instance metadata and apply a kernel hint; compatibility fallback uses current selector when hint absent or scores stale.
Links: design doc: https://confluence.internal.redwood/inference/prefill-handshake-microbench; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345
acceptance_criteria:
1) Handshake runs within configured budget on 95% of instance types (< 300ms wall time observed).
2) Preference vector written to instance metadata and read by routing layer under feature flag.
3) In canary fleet, p95 prefill latency improves by >=8% for medium-length (32-256) requests without increasing p99 for other flows.
4) No measurable increase in GPU contention or SLO violations in probe windows.
5) e2e integration tests + load test dashboards created and linked.
comments: 2025-02-19 - Ava Chen: Kickoff meeting summary. Agreed to prioritize low-budget probes and to reuse existing microbench harness code. Action: Mateo to prototype the adapter and wire a metadata schema. Linked design doc.

2025-02-22 - Mateo Ruiz: Prototype complete. Runs a 6x3 matrix (6 seqlen buckets x 3 kernels) and reports tokens/sec and median/95 latency. Observed that flash kernel has lower median for 64/128 but higher variance on 512 for Ampere A10G. Initial probe cost ~180ms.

2025-02-24 - Grace Park (SRE): Concern about running probes during high GPU utilization. Added pre-probe gating: skip if GPU util > 60% or if there are existing latency anomalies. Also set probe to exponential backoff when skipped.

2025-02-26 - Performance lab: Small-scale canary (n=50 instances) against the baseline selector. Results: p95 prefill latency reduced by 9% in targeted buckets; decode per-token unchanged. Memory pressure negligible. Uploaded raw runs: https://internal-dashboards/redwood/runtime/probes/483999.

2025-02-28 - PM review (Jordan Li): Approved to expand to broader fleet for 72-hour soak. PM asked for additional telemetry: store pre-probe seqlen histogram anchor and probe_reason in metadata. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-03-01 - Mateo Ruiz: Implemented TTL of 24h for preference vectors and drift detection using Jensen-Shannon divergence threshold 0.2 on seqlen histograms. Pushed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345. Preparing rollout playbook.
TODO - Next: run 72-hour soak, collect customer impact metrics, finalize rollout doc, add automated rollback if probe causes >0.5% SLO regression.
